definition: Defines the method by which the annotation was created. Clinically_derived - Based on information produced in the process of the subject's medical care; Retrospective_expert - Based on information produced retrospective to the subject's care by annotators with relevant special clinical expertise; Retrospective_general - Based on information produced retrospective to the subject's care by annotators without relevant special clinical expertise; Retrospective_auto - Based on information produced retrospective to the subject's care using automated means.

The name of the annotation. These names are unique and assigned by MIDRC. Annotation names reference a document posted on the MIDRC website describing the annotation, methods and values expected.  All MIDRC created annotations start with "midrc_".
Coded value to represent a particular annotator in a group. These need only be unique per annotation.
A list of one or more case submitter_ids associated with this data.
The submitter_id or id of the core_metadata_collection to which the rf_series_file belongs, i.e., a link to a record in the parent node.
A combination of date and time of day in the form [-]CCYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss[Z|(+|-)hh:mm]
The category of the annotation file. Must be "DICOM Annotation Series File".
The file format of the annotation file, e.g., JSON.
An indication of whether the annotation is expert validated by MIDRC (“Internal Annotation”) or has not be validated by MIDRC experts (“External Annotation”).
Type of error for the data file object.
The name (or part of a name) of a file (of any type).
The size of the data file (object) in bytes.
The current state of the data file object.

A 128-bit identifier. Depending on the mechanism used to generate it, it is either guaranteed to be different from all other UUIDs/GUIDs generated until 3400 AD or extremely likely to be different. Its relatively small size lends itself well to sorting, ordering, and hashing of all sorts, storing in databases, simple allocation, and ease of programming in general.
The submitter_id or id of the imaging_study this annotation relates to, i.e., a link to a record in the parent node.
(0008, 0070) Manufacturer
(0008, 1090) Manufacturer's Model Name
The 128-bit hash value expressed as a 32 digit hexadecimal number used as a file's digital fingerprint.
(0008, 0060) Modality
The GUID of the object in the index service.
Unique ID for any specific defined piece of work that is undertaken or attempted to meet a single requirement.
(0008, 103e) Series Description; a general description of or additional information about the imaging series. If possible, the Series Description should match the annotation_name provided.
(0020, 000e) Series Instance UID; the UID or unique identification code of the imaging series.
(0018,1020) Software Versions. This is the software version of the application where the annotation series was created.
The current state of the object.
A human-readable, unique identifier for a record in the metadata database. It can be used in place of the UUID for identifying or recalling a record (e.g., in data queries or uploads/exports).
The node_id of the node in the data model; the name of the node used in queries and API requests (e.g., "aligned_reads_file" for the "Aligned Reads File" node).
A combination of date and time of day in the form [-]CCYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss[Z|(+|-)hh:mm]
Version of the submitting theranostics extension, independently of the MIDRC baseline version.
Record curation state, independent of clinical value.
Identifier of the originating source record; use an approved pseudonym when needed.
Source system or data provider.
Names of properties missing from this record; no missing value is encoded as zero.
Reasons corresponding by index to missing_properties.
SHA-256 checksum of the immutable artifact.
Format or standard release, including PETSIRD version where relevant.
Profile used to de-identify file contents and metadata.
